beats.text: Banks made six billion dollars in one year from people with no money.
And the ones who paid it had the least.
So why does being broke cost more than being rich?
You will see who is cashing in and why toilet paper proves it.
Meet my bank account which right now holds four dollars and it is the most loyal thing in my life.
Rent is due on Friday and I am out of toilet paper so I walk into the store.
The big pack is cheaper per roll but it costs more today and today I have four dollars.
So I buy the small pack and I just paid extra for being broke.
Researchers at the University of Michigan checked this and poor families pay about five and a half percent more for every roll.
Rich families catch the sale more often because they have spare cash on the day the sale happens.
It is not that poor people are bad at math because the math is easy when you have the money.
And a few cents on toilet paper sounds tiny until you see what the bank does with the same four dollars.
I walk into the bank to open a savings account like a responsible adult.
The paper says I need five hundred dollars just to keep the account free.
That is the number one reason people in America have no bank account at all.
So I keep my account with no minimum and then my card goes one dollar below zero.
Have a guess what one dollar below zero costs me.
Thirty five dollars for a one dollar mistake.
Banks in America collected five point eight billion dollars from fees like this in one year.
And here is the twist because back in twenty nineteen it was almost twelve billion.
Rules and public anger cut it in half and the average family that overdrafts now keeps about one hundred eighty five dollars a year.
Good news for my four dollars except that when the bank says no there is another door right across the street.
Friday comes and the rent is still due and my paycheck is still a week away.
The payday loan shop gives me cash in ten minutes and I only pay fifteen dollars for every hundred.
Fifteen percent sounds like a bad deal but not a monster.
Except the loan lasts only two weeks so over a whole year that price is almost four hundred percent.
A credit card for someone with money is around twenty and this is twenty times worse.
And when the two weeks end most people do not have the money so they borrow again to pay the first loan.
Now I am paying a fee to pay a fee for a fee and my four dollars has left the chat.
So here is the toilet paper secret I promised you because it was never about the toilet paper.
The store and the bank and the loan shop all charge the most to the person with the least spare cash.
But there is one thing all three are scared of and it costs less than a pizza.
So why does being broke cost more than being rich?
You would think the answer is just earn more money.
Nope because the real price tag is not on your income but on your cushion.
When you have no cushion every small problem gets sold back to you at the highest price in town.
And the thing they are all scared of is a tiny emergency fund that starts with twenty dollars.
Twenty dollars set aside means no overdraft and no loan shop and one day the big pack of toilet paper.
My four dollars is now my four dollars plus sixteen and it feels like a fortress.
Now tell me in the comments what is the most expensive thing about being broke where you live.
I am Dave and my four dollars and I will see you next time.
